INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science &
Technology, Environment & Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on
its behalf, present this Two Hundred and Eighty- ninth report on the Action Taken by the Department
of Science & Technology on the recommendations contained in Two Hundred and Eighty-first Report
of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2016-2017) of the Department of Science & Technology,
which was presented/laid in the both the Houses of Parliament on 9th May, 2016.
2. There were eighteen recommendations in the Two Hundred and Eighty-first Report of the Committee.
Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on
12th August, 2016.
3. In the meeting held on 29th November, 2016, the Committee considered the draft Report and
adopted the same.
   N
EW D ELHI; RENUKA CHOWDHURY
1 December, 2016 Chairperson,
Agrahayana 10, 1938 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science & Technology, Environment & Forests,
Rajya Sabha.

(iv)
ACRONYMS
DST : Department of Science & Technology
IIA : Indian Institute of Astrophysics
IMPRINT : Impacting Research Innovation & Technology
NA TMO : National Thematic Mapping Organisation
NLST : National Large Solar Telescope
SERB : Sci ence and Engineering Research Board
SoI : Survey of India

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science &
Technology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Eighty first Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests
on the Demands for Grants (2016-17) of the Department of Science & Technology, presented to both
the Houses of Parliament on 9th May, 2016. There were eighteen recommendations in the Two Hundred
and eighty-first Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee
were received from the Department on 12th August, 2016.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
Action Taken by the Department of Science & Technology are set out in the following paragraphs:-
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2016-17
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of rationalisation and merger of some Heads and hopes that new merged
Heads will provide the required flexibility to the Department to run its schemes. (Para 7.3)
Action Taken by Government
No action required.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee expresses satisfaction over increase in budgetary allocation to the Department of
Science & Technology this year and maintaining the same level of allocation at R.E. Stage
2015-16 and hopes that enhanced allocation will be optimally utilised. The Committee is also
hopeful that the Department will make efficient use of allocated funds in a transparent and
objective manner so that targets set by the Department are achieved. (Para 7.6)
Action Taken by Government
Observation of the Committee has been noted.
Comments
The Committee would appreciate an affirmative commitment in the Action Taken note.

2
NEW INITIATIVES
Recommendation
The Committee welcomes the joint collaborative steps taken by the DST in association with Ministry
of Human Resources Development to implement Impacting Research Innovation & Technology
(IMPRINT) Projects and hopes that this collaboration will help much needed societal and
developmental needs. (Para 8.6)
Action Taken by Government
No action required.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee welcomes the initiatives taken to make India clean, healthy and global manufacturing
hub. The Committee also values the partnership of the Department of Science & Technology with
the Ministries of Railways and Human Resource Development, Departments of Heavy Industry and
Electronics and Information Technology and hopes that such efforts would give much needed philip
to the Railways and provide much needed capacity building in Human Resource Sector. The Committee
hopes that these initiatives will help India become cleaner and healthier. The Committee also hopes
that adequate budgetary provisions will be made for these ambitious schemes. (Para 8.13)
Action Taken by Government
Observation of the Committee has been noted.
Comments
The Committee expects that the Department gives details of the action taken on the
observation instead of simply noting it.
Recommendation
The Committee hopes that “Make In India” Programme will help India attain leadership in global
manufacturing. The Committee recommends that considering the significance of the initiative, the
Department should make every possible effort in assisting the lead Ministries for the success of the
Programme. The Committee also recommends that allocated outlays to the Department for the
Programme are fully utilised to make the Programme a success. (Para 8.14)
Action Taken by Government
The Department agrees with recommendations of the Committee. The Department will extend
appropriate advisory and technical support to lead Ministries for the success of the “Make in India”

3
Programme as per their demand and requirement. The Department will take sincere steps to utilize
allocated outlays fully to make the programme a success.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply. The Committee is hopeful that with necessary
support of the Department, the lead Ministries will make ‘Make In India’ Programme a success.
TREND OF UTILISATION IN THE LAST THREE YEARS
Recommendation
The Committee finds that though utilisation of allocated resources by the Department improved
considerably in the last three years, however budget has remained underutilised in 8 schemes. As
on 21st March, 2016, the Department could not utilise a quarter of funds allocated to aforementioned
eight schemes. The Committee notes underutilisation by the Department under these schemes and
would like the Department to improve its performance in terms of utilisation of funds.
(Para 9.5)
Action Taken by Government
The utilization of allocated budget is now being regularly monitored at the level of Secretary on
fortnightly basis and specific instructions are being given to the concerned Division Heads to meet the
monthly and quarterly utilization targets. Where underutilization is expected due to various reasons
beyond the control of the Department, allocation of funds to other schemes where these are needed more
will be done at the earliest possible.
Comments
Reply of the Department is noted. The Committee is hopeful that with monitoring of
utilisation of allocated budget at highest level on fortnightly basis, the Department would be able
to timely complete its projects and fully utilise the resources allocated.
Recommendation
The Committee, thus, is of the view that grounds cited by the Department are of routine administrative
nature which could have been avoided by the Department as delay in completion of infrastructure
projects leads to time and cost overrun and affects Research & Development work. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the loopholes which led to underutilisation of funds should be plugged
and delay in seeking administrative approval should be avoided. (Para 9.7)
Action Taken by Government
Observation of the Committee has been noted. In the fortnightly review by the Secretary, way and
means to plug loopholes and avoid delays are also discussed and decision on measures to expedite
utilization is being taken regularly.

4
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that robust monitoring would ensure effective
utilisation of resources and timely completion of projects.
MODERNISATION OF MAPPING ORGANIZATIONS (SOI AND NATMO)
Recommendations
The Committee notes that the Department is undertaking modernisation and upgradation of
infrastructure and technical capabilities of Survey of India and NATMO under the programme
“Modernisation of Mapping Organisations”. The Committee, however, notes that during the last
few years, the Department repeatedly failed to fully utilise funds made available to it under this
programme. The Committee is of the opinion that gross underutilisation of resources allocated,
presents a bad image of the Survey of India and NATMO. The fact that these organisations could
not utilise a quarter of funds allocated for their upgradation speaks volumes about their commitment
to do so. As per information furnished by the Department, it could utilise only 52.02% of the budget
allocated in 2015-16 under Modernisation of Mapping Organisations by 21st March, 2016.
(Paras 10.8 & 10.9)
The Committee, therefore, expresses its strong displeasure that the Department has not even been
able to fully utilise funds meant for up gradation of infrastructure of its two important organisations and
recommends that the Department should take all necessary measures to increase spend ability in order
to ensure timely and successful implementation of this programme.
Action Taken by Government
Two modernisation projects of Survey of India could not be got approved and hence the utilization
remained on the lower side. These projects are scheduled for approval before September 2016. It is also
proposed to fast track implementation of these projects so that funds allocated for 2016-17 under
Modernisation of Mapping Organisations are fully utilized. The organisations, especially Survey of India,
have been asked to streamline their procedures and implementation processes to ensure full utilization of
funds this year. The Surveyor General has been asked to get in touch personally with highest authorities
in CPWD and State Government Department to ensure timely completion of all major and minor works.
The Survey of India has reported that they have started monthly review meetings with these authorities
at different stations.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. The Committee however would like to be apprised of the
progress achieved on a regular basis.
MEGA FACILITIES FOR BASIC RESEARCH
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken and infrastructure developed under Mega Facilities
for Basic Research in collaboration with national and international agencies. However, since

5
permission of Ministry of Defence has now been received for availability of the Merak site in
Ladakh, the Committee hopes that new roadmap for creating infrastructure will be drawn at the
earliest and the National Large Solar Telescope will established at the earliest. The Committee also
recommends that necessary budgetary provision should be made for creating such Mega facilities.
(Para 11.4)
Action Taken by Government
The National Large Solar Telescope (NLST) project is steered by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics
(IIA), Bengaluru at the national level. Subsequent to the Department of Science & Technology (DST)
receiving the clearance from the Ministry of Defence for the Merak site in Ladakh for installing the
NLST, IIA has applied for the environmental clearance. The matter was considered by the Standing
Committee of State Board for Wildlife, J&K Government after internal evaluation. The Standing Committee
of State Board for Wildlife, J&K Government held its meeting on 18th May 2016 at Srinagar. Its
recommendations will be submitted to the National Board for final clearance. IIA has also applied for
acquiring land in the proposed area on lease. A detailed site plan for the Merak site and updated Detailed
Project Report are presently under preparation.
Comments
The Committee takes notes of the reply and hopes that National Large Solar Telescope and
other Mega facilities will be completed as per schedule.
Recommendation
The Committee is disappointed with the fact that India could not achieve associate membership of
the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN), Geneva and fund to the tune of Rs. 30.00
crores remained unutilised under the Programme. The Department has cited that Associate Membership
of CERN could not be achieved due to elaborate formalities at CERN’ s end. The Committee is not
convinced by the logic put forward by the Department and is of the view that the Department should
have anticipated the time taken in completion of formalities at international institutions. However,
the Committee hopes that with the enhanced allocation of Rs. 120 crores, Department of Science
& Technology will be able to achieve its targets under Mega facilities for Basic Research and will
make concerted efforts to achieve Associate Membership of CERN, Geneva without any further
delay. (Para 11.6)
Action Taken by Government
The application for India’s Associate Membership of CERN has considerably advanced. We have
now received the draft Model Agreement from CERN. The Agreements are under examination in India
for signature. It is expected that the whole process will be completed by October, 2016 after a vote by
the CERN Council. The fee for Associate Membership of CERN will have to be paid thereafter. The
process for India to become an Associate Member of CERN is on course.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and hopes that India will soon join CERN as an
Associate Member.

6
LASER INTERFEROMETER GRA VITATIONAL-WA VE OBSERVATORY (LIGO)
Recommendation
The Committee believes that the proposed LIGO-India project has tremendous potential to unravel
the myriad mysteries of the universe. It is likely to become a tool for the Indian astronomy in
keeping up the level of excellence in research in astronomy and astrophysics of the country. The
Committee hopes that the LIGO-India project would help the country to embark on world class
international science collaborations and help India become a force to reckon with in this field.
(Para 12.6)
Action Taken by Government
The Department of Science & Technology and the Department of Atomic Energy are grateful for
the observations of the Standing Committee that LIGO-India could become a major development in the
field of gravitational wave astronomy once the LIGO detector is established in India. Over 50 scientists
and research students from different institutions in the country are already actively participating in the
project. Site Selection Committee has finalised its recommendations, and shortly, a pre-project proposal
for acquisition of land and other prototyping activities is expected to be placed for approval of the
competent authority. In parallel, design work on the LIGO-India set-up in collaboration with US counterparts
is continuing.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the progress made in the matter.
DRUGS AND PHARMACEUTICAL RESEARCH PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee taking serious note of the above observations made by the CAG and massive
underutilisation of funds under the Programme recommends that these deficiencies need to be
addressed by the Department in right earnest as such cases bring disrepute to the Drugs &
Pharmaceutical Programme and this does not put Department in right stead. (Para 13.8)
Action Taken by Government
In compliance of observations of the Committee, Department is in the process of streamlining
procedures to ensure full utilization of funds.
Comments
The Committee, while taking note of the reply, hopes that deficiencies in this Programme
will be addressed in right earnest. The Committee would also like to be apprised of the progress
made in the process of streamlining procedure to ensure full utilisation of funds when the
procedures are actually streamlined.

7
REV AMPING OF SCIENCE EXPRESS
Recommendation
The Committee welcomes the revamping of the Science Express in its new avatar of ‘Science
Express: Climate Change Special’. The Committee hopes that the joint collaboration of Ministries
of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and Railways; Departments of Science and Technology
and Biotechnology will show encouraging results in spreading awareness about the challenges posed
by Climate Change. The Committee also feels that there is a need for crowd management in a better
way in the Science Express and more such trains should be introduced so that viewers get more time
for viewing. (Para 14.6)
Action Taken by Government
It is accepted that there is a need for crowd management in a better way. In this regard, DST is
adding 2 new coaches in the next phase. During its run, platform activities, outreach programmes will
be organised. Press coverage through print and electronic will also take place as before.
For the recommendation on introduction of more such trains, the Department is examining the
feasibility to have another train considering that mobile exhibition buses are also running.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and hopes that the steps taken by the Department
will increase the outreach of the Science Express.
EFFORTS FOR RETAINING RESEARCH TALENT IN THE COUNTRY
Recommendation
The Committee notes the initiatives taken by the Department of Science & Technology that have
resulted in brain-gain of 235 accomplished scientists to India. The Committee recommends that further
measures should be taken to attract Indian scientists to comeback to India. For that purpose, the
Department should further increase the scholarship/stipends provided to researchers and incentivise
performance based research. (Para 15.5)
Action Taken by Government
The Department is committed to attract the Indian brain from abroad and continue its attempt to
retain them to pursue world class research in Indian setting. The ongoing Ramanujan Fellowship of the
Department for brilliant scientists and engineers from all over the world to take up scientific research
positions in India has received utmost attention and the number of awards is increasing steadily. The
fellowship amount and the Research Grant had also been made more attractive. As recommended by the
Committee to increase the scholarship and stipend provided to researchers, the Government has enhanced
the fellowship of Junior Research Fellows, Senior Research Fellows and Research Associates to the tune

8
of 55.5% to 66.7% w.e.f. October, 2014. The Early Career Research Grant Scheme and National
Postdoctoral Fellowship Scheme of the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) are linked to
the potential and performance of the research undertaken; and substantial funding is provided under these
Schemes. Track based research funding Scheme of the SERB is designed to support active scientists
based on their performance and utility of research.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
MECHANISM TO MONITOR AND REVIEW THE ONGOING SCHEMES
Recommendation
The Committee notes the mechanism devised by the Department of Science & Technology to monitor
and evaluate the progress of various schemes. However, the Committee feels that had the monitoring
mechanism of the Department been so robust, underutilisation would not have taken place under
some schemes particularly in Modernisation of Mapping Organisations. (Para 16.2)
Action Taken by Government
As already submitted, the utilization of funds is now being reviewed on fortnightly basis by the
Secretary and it is expected that during the financial year 2016-17, there will be marked improvement.
Comments
The Committee is hopeful that with monitoring of utilisation of allocated resources on
fortnightly basis at the highest level, the Department would manage to complete its projects on
time and fully utilise the precious resources.
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that there is a considerable scope for improvement in the performance
of the Department and in the light of adverse audit observations made by the Controller & Auditor
General particularly on Drugs & Pharmaceutical Research Programme, the Department needs to
strengthen its monitoring mechanism so that misuse of funds could be prevented and timely completion
of projects and optimum utilisation of funds could be ensured. (Para 16.3)
Action Taken by Government
The observation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.
Comments
The Committee would like to be apprised when actual compliance is made along with the
results achieved.

9
Recommendation
It is high time that the Department of Science and Technology strives to be on par with international
standards in the long run in terms of the speed and quantum of scientific and technological
breakthroughs in order to expeditiously realise India’s rightful place as a global leader in various
domains of science and technology including particularly supercomputing. (Para 16.4)
Action Taken by Government
The Department has noted the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee and
would make all efforts to meet the expectations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee expressed

: APPENDIX-I
Questionnaire on the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess (Amendment) Bill, 1995

1. To what extent has the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
hitherto been able to:

(a) augment the resources of the Central and State Pollution Control Boards/
Committees (normal budget + additionality due to the cess)?

(b) prevent and control pollution?
(c) minimise indiscriminate consumption of water?

2. What is the justification for enlisting only 16 categories of industry in Schedule I of the
Act for cess collection?

3. Whether the Schedule | (list of specified industries) should be deleted and all
industries/activities consuming water exceeding certain limit should be made liable to pay
cess?

4, Whether the Schedule II should continue as it is or it should be simplified?

5. Whether the rates for levying cess are commensurate with the objective of promoting
installation of water pollution control systems and for water conservation? If not, what are
your suggestions in this regard?

6. What, according to you, should be the criteria for deciding whether an industrial unit is
to be assessed for cess?

7. Whether the existing procedure for giving a rebate of 25 per cent of the cess, as
provided in the Cess Act, 1977, amended in 1991, needs any modification?

8. Whether the Pollution Control Boards are facing any difficulty in collection of cess? If
so, what are the difficulties?

9. Whether the industry/municipalities have any objection regarding payment of cess? If
so, what are the details thereof?

10. What is the formula for redistribution of cess to the Central and State Pollution
Control Boards/Pollution Control Committees (at the U.T. level)? Whether any modifications
are required, and if so, what steps have been taken in this regard?

11. What are the activities in which the State Pollution Control Boards / Pollution
Control Committees utilise the cess money?

12. What is the financial support provided to the State Pollution Control Boards/
Committees by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations in
addition to the funds received through cess redistribution from the Central Government?

13. In what manner should the principle of “polluter pays” be applied in the case of
levying of cess?

14. What are the reasons for levying of cess on units concerned with hydel power
generation when it neither causes pollution nor involves indiscriminate use of water?

15. What is your view on the levying of cess for domestic consumers?

16. What is the amount of cess being presently collected under the Act and what is the
anticipated collection after the proposed amendment becomes effective?


17. If the use of water for domestic purpose is not included in category I and is kept as
a separate category as earlier, what difference does it make?

18. Under the proposed amendment in Schedule II, maximum rates under sub-Section
(2-A) of Section 3 of the Act of 1977 have been prescribed but does this section also apply
to those industrial units as well who default in payment of cess levied on them?


APPENDIX-II(i)
Reply to the Questionnaire furnished by the Ministry of Environment & Forests

ANS. 1(a): Water Cess collection is the most significant source of financing for State
Pollution Control Boards. Some State Boards are entirely dependent on the Cess for their
resources. The total Cess collection during the year 1992-93 was Rs. 26.77 crores and in
1993-94 it was Rs. 31.56 crores.

The Central Pollution Control Board is not provided any financial support from the
Cess collections. The Central Board receives grant-in-aid from the Ministry of Environment
& Forests for its plan and non-plan activities.

1(b)&(c): Under the Cess Act, each of the industries included in the schedule is subject
to two different rates of cess. Where the assessee treats its water borne effluents to the
standards prescribed for the industry, a lower rate of Cess is applicable. If not, higher rate is
enforced. Further, a rebate is given if the industrial unit adopts water conserving technology
These provisions act as incentives in reducing pollution

The Cess is levied on the quantity of water consumed by the industry. To reduce the
Cess payable, industries are thus made to consume less water than would otherwise be the
case.

ANS. 2: The 16 categories of industries included in Schedule-I are such selected
industries which use water in large quantities, and generate heavy pollution load. The list
has been subject to modifications from time to time.

ANS. 3: The 16 categories of industries in Schedule-I are selected on the basis of the
quantity of water they consume. The list has been subject to modifications from time to
time. The Central and State Pollution Control Boards have suggested that Schedule-1 may
be deleted and the Cess Act be made applicable to water consuming industries / activities if
the water consumption is beyond a certain limit (20 KL/day).

ANS. 4: The existing schedule-II is already simple and there is no need to further
simplify it. The categorisation of industries is based on the purpose for which water is
consumed and also on the nature of the pollutants generated.

ANS. 5: Ideally, the rates of Cess should be such that the industry should find it
economical to instal pollution control systems and adopt water conservation measures rather
than pay the Cess. But this would mean raising the rates to very high levels compared to the
present levels. This would also show that the Cess rates need to be enhanced.

ANS. 6: The major criteria for deciding 35.10 whether an industrial unit is to be assessed
for Cess are the quantity of water consumed by it and the pollution load discharged by it.

ANS. 7: Earlier, rebate of 70 per cent was given for installation of effluent treatment
plants. It was since reduced to 25 per cent. The exact percentage can be determined only
through .detailed case studies for each industry.

ANS. 8: The following difficulties are being faced by the Boards:
— Local Authorites do not pay Cess;

— There are problems in actual assessment of water consumption due to lack of
installation of water metering devices.

ANS. 9: Some industries like sugar mills and power utilities have raised objection


against payment of Cess on the ground that either they are not covered under the Cess Act or
that they do not cause any pollution. The municipalities have not raised any objection.

ANS. 10: As per the existing formula:

— 25 per cent of Cess is to be retained by the Central Government for installation of
sewage treatment plants and adoption of cleaner technologies;

— 25 per cent of Cess to be utilised by the State Boards for sewage treatment and adoption
of clean technologies;

— 25 per cent of Cess to be utilised for pollution control programmes as per decision of
State Governmenv/State Board.

— 25 per cent of Cess as incentive against achieving set targets (15 per cent against 85 per
cent target and additional one per cent against more than 85 per cent target).

The SPCBs/Committees have petitioned that the redistribution formula should be changed
from the existing one under which 75 per cent is reimbursed to the SPCBs/Committees to one
where 80 per cent is reimbursed to SPCBs/Committees. Ministry of finanace has agreed in
principle to the formula of 80/20 and necessary orders are being issued. This formula will be
effective from 1995-96.

ANS. 11: The Cess money is utilised for strengthening the institutional capacities of
Pollution Control Boards and their day-to-day functioning. This includes:

— Enforcement work;

— Surveys;

With reference to the letter cited, I am to furnish the following suggestion to scrap the
Schedule-I of the Cess Act.

The basic object of the Cess Act is to conserve the water resources, maintain and
restore its wholesomeness, Prevent and Control its pollution. Thus the ‘Cess Act is a
disincentive for the indiscriminate consumption of Water and Pollution thereon. As such, the
Cess Act should be applicable to every type of use of Water so that maximum economy in
its use is achieved. This can be done only by enlarging the scope of the Cess Act.

The Cess Act specifies the industries in Schedule-I appended to the Act which are liable
to pay cess. The types of industries have been specified and categorised in very wide terms.
The item No. (1) of the Schedule-I i.e., ‘Ferrous Metallurgical Industry’ covers all the
industries where the metals are separated from their ores, making and compounding alloys
and working or heat treating metals so as to give them certain desired shapes or properties.
But the industries are challenging its applicability under the umbrealla of some judicial
pronouncement where it has been declared that in Tax statutes the meaning of the words
should be construed in its popular sense rather than its wider dense or dictionery meaning.
Sugar Industry was alleging that sugarcane is not a vegetable (in its popular sense) and so, it
does not fall under item 15 of Schedule-I namely processing of ‘animal and vegetable
products industry’. Subsequently, the Cese Rules, were amended to read the item ‘15’ of
Schedule-I as ‘Processing of milk, meat, hides and skins, all agricultural products and their
wastes’ by which ‘sugar Industry’ comes under the purview of Cess Act.

Similarly, some large and medium scale industries have considerable labour strength
which consume large quantities of water for demestic purposes and they also consume large
quantities of water for industrial cooling, boiler feed, etc. But these industries are contesting
that they do not come under the provisions of Cess Act simply because the list of industries
furnished in Schedule-] does not cover their types of activity.


Thus the basic object of Cess Act namely Conservation of water resources fails. Hence
it is suggested that the Schedule-I which specifies industries which are liable to pay cess may
be scrapped. Instead, the industries consuming less than 100KL/Month for both domestic
and industrial purposes may be exempted since the overhead charges namely, stationery,
postage, etc. involved in the collection of meagre amounts of cess will be more than that of
the collections from these industries.

Hence I request you to take up above matter with the Ministry of Environment &
Forests, Government of India to scrap Schedule-I of the Cess Act. Meanwhile Hotels and
Restaurants, may be included in the Schedule-I since scrapping of schedule requires
amendment to the Cess Act.

deposited with the Government of India, Ministry of Environment and they reimburse only

contributes towards their not being fully capable of controlling the pollution effectively.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Atomic
Energy on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Eighty Second Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment &
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2016-17) of the Department of Atomic Energy, which was
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 9th May, 2016. The Committee had in all made
twenty two recommendations/observations in the report.  Action Taken Note on the report was
received by the Committee on 19th September, 2016.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on
the Action Taken by the Department of Atomic Energy are set out in the following paragraphs:-
MAJOR PROGRAMMES
Recommendation
The Committee notes with satisfaction that in the last sixty two years of its existence, the
Department of Atomic Energy has mastered a host of highly complex technologies particularly in
the field of medical radiology, nuclear agriculture, desalination, food irradiation, radio astronomy,
supercomputing, particle accelerators, plasma and cryogenics. True to the visions of Dr. Homi J.
Bhabha and Jawaharlal Nehru of envisaging the usage of atomic energy to make a difference to
the social life of Indians, the DAE should now strive to scale it up and take it to the next level.
The Committee feels that the share of nuclear power which accounts for only 3.3 per cent of
India’ s total electricity generation, needs to be increased to the higher proportions and efforts
should be made in this direction. (Para 2.7)
Action Taken by Government
The views of the honourable Committee are noted.
The Government has taken a host of measures to increase nuclear power generation and its
share in the country’s electricity production. These include:
z Agreements with foreign countries for setting up of Light Water Reactors (LWRs);
z Provision of fuel in required quantity (from both domestic and imported sources) to
ensure that the reactors are operated at rated power by opening of new mines and
processing facilities, and also by signing fuel supply contracts with several countries for
import of fuel for reactors under IAEA safeguards. In respect of future projects to be
set up with international cooperation, lifetime fuel supply guarantees are being
incorporated in commercial contracts;
z ‘In-Principle’ approval of sites of proposed reactors;
z Creation of Indian Nuclear Insurance Pool (INIP) and obtaining of Insurance policy by

2
operator for meeting its liability under the Civil Liability for  Nuclear  Damage  (CLND)
Act-2010;
z Amendment of the Atomic Energy Act to facilitate Joint Venture companies to set up
nuclear power plants;
z Recent budget speech announcement by the Honourable Finance Minister to augment
investment in nuclear power over a period of 15 years.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
FINANCIAL PROGRESS IN TWELFTH FIVE YEAR PLAN
Recommendation
The Committee takes serious view of the fact that in the first four years of current Plan
nearly 55.74% of the allocations have been disbursed. The major share i.e. 44.25% of the
allocation has accumulated for the remaining one year. Even if the Department is disbursed entire
amount, it seems impossible to utilise 44% of the plan allocation during the remaining one year .
While taking serious view of the fact that pro-rata allocations are not made annually, the
Committee recommends that in the remaining one year of the Plan period, allocations should be
made and utilised on pro-rata basis to catch up the Plan targets. The Department also needs to
improve upon the utilisation of funds. (Para 6.4)
Action Taken by Government
The observation of the honorable Committee is noted. In this regard, the following are further
submitted :-
With the approval of Ministry of Finance, funds were re-appropriated from Demand No.4 to
Demand No.5 and the Department could utilise 97% of the plan  budget allocations, in 2015-16.
Further, merger of Demand  No.5  with Demand  No.4 and Rationalisation of the Schemes,
are  likely to improve the capacity  of the Department in utilisation of the budget allocation. Review
meetings have been conducted by Secretary / Additional Secretary  periodically. In addition to
monitoring of the Project/Schemes, scrutiny at micro level is also being undertaken.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like the Department to pursue the
matter with Ministry of Finance for disbursement of full XII Five Y ear Plan allocation.
UTILISATION OF THE APPROVED OUTLAY IN 2015-16
Recommendation
On overall analysis, the Committee finds that Plan expenditure by the Department under
Atomic Energy and Nuclear Power scheme is satisfactory but there is considerable scope to improve
upon the performance because Actual utilisation of funds in Plan schemes is 93% of corresponding
period the previous year. (Para 7.3)

3
Action Taken by Government
The observations  of the honorable Committee are  noted.  Action plan has been  chalked
out to improve upon the performance.
Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has been utilizing the funds provided
to it by the Government almost completely excepting that provided for Neighborhood Development
Programme (NDP) - Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project (KKNPP). With regard to NDP, utilization
of funds is subject to progress of work of  housing which is being implemented by the
Government of Tamil Nadu.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like the Department to constantly monitor
the utilisation of funds.
Recommendation
The Committee observes that there is a tendency of underutilisation under Nuclear Power
Schemes. During the Demands for Grants meeting the Committee was provided explanation for
underutilisation in Demand No. 5. The Committee understands the logic put forward by the
Department. The Committee takes note of Merger of Demand no. 5 (Nuclear Power Scheme with
Demand No. - 4 (Atomic Energy Programmes) and hopes that merger of the two schemes will result
in better utilisation of precious budgetary resources. (Para 7.5)
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the honourable Committee are noted.
Periodical Reviews have been introduced at the department, unit and divisions level to ensure
better utilisation of precious budgetary resources.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the monitoring at micro level and hopes that this will
result in increased utilisation of allocated resources.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION IN 2016-17
Recommendation
The Committee feels that reduction at B.E. to the tune of
 `  6538.16 Crore against the
projected outlay of  `  25,220.64 crore and especially to the tune of  `  4613.11 crore under Plan
Head against projected Plan BE of  `  10813.11 crore is unjustified. It has adversely impacted the
Plan and Non plan projects of the Department particularly reduction in Non-Plan allocation as it
affects the day-to-day functioning of the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Ministry of Finance should consider the proposal for increase in outlay at RE stage particularly
under Non Plan Research & Development, Industries and Minerals Sectors. (Para 9.5)
Action Taken by Government
Department accepts the observations of the honorable Committee and  the same shall be
brought to the notice of Ministry of Finance for their kind consideration at RE 2016-17 stage.

4
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of the progress made in
the matter.
Recommendation
The Committee welcomes the additional allocation of 3000.00 crore by the Finance Minister
in his budget speech under clean energy Programme and the recommends that in the area of critical
national importance and clean energy, the Ministry of Finance should give maximum financial
support for the programmes of the Department under the appropriate financing mechanism.
(Para 9.6)
Action Taken by Government
Department accepts the recommendations of the honourable Committee. Department in
consultation with Ministry of Finance is working out the appropriate financing mechanism.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to  be apprised of the progress made

5

BHABHA ATOMIC RESEARCH CENTRE (BARC)
Financial Performance
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the activities undertaken by BARC and allocation of
 `  2850.75
crore under Power , Industries and Research & Development Sector and hopes that a concrete action
plan would be prepared to fully utilise the allocated budgetary resources and important projects

Efforts are being made for optimum utilization of budgetary allocations. Project & expenditure

The Committee notes the fact that BARC had utilized 96% of RE allocation in 2015-16
and hopes that the BARC will continue utilising its entire allocated budget.
Recommendation
The Committee notes the important contributions made by the BARC in providing potable
water to people, reprocessing and waste management and supercomputing. The Committee is hopeful
that BARC will maintain its service of ensuring delivery of fruits of nuclear science & technology
to the common people. (Para 11.12)
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Honorable Committee are noted.  The following activities are being
progressed :-
1. Providing Portable Water to People:
(i) One technology on high solute rejecting reverse osmosis membrane has been
developed and transferred to private entrepreneur for commercial scale production
and deployment. These membranes are capable of desalinating seawater.
(ii) The technology of online domestic water purifier based on ultrafiltration membrane
has been transferred to Vishwakarma Institute of Technology, Pune under AKRUTI
program of DAE for deployment in the rural areas.
2. Supercomputing :
BARC has embarked on an ambitious programme of developing supercomputing capacity
of 1000 Teraflops as a part of its XII plan activities. It has developed ANUPAM-AGGRA

6
parallel supercomputer in 2013 which had sustained performance of 110 Teraflops. In
2016, BARC has developed a new supercomputer ANUPAM - AGANYA which has
sustained performance of 270 Teraflops. BARC will continue to develop state-of-art
supercomputers indigenously which will aid the scientific community to solve
challenging problems and result in tangible benefits to the society.
3. Reprocessing and Waste Management:
India, has adopted “closed fuel cycle” and treats spent nuclear fuel as a material of
resource. 99% of the material in spent fuel is useful material. The closed fuel cycle
aims at optimum utilisation of fuel resources by reprocessing of spent fuel, recovering
U and Pu from spent fuel and recycling them to reactor as fuel. This finally leads to
a very small percentage of residual material present in spent nuclear fuel requiring better
management as radioactive waste.
Safe management of nuclear waste has been accorded highest priority right from the
inception of our nuclear energy programme. As a waste management philosophy, no
waste in any physical form is released / disposed off  to the environment unless the
same is cleared, exempted or excluded from regulations. A comprehensive radioactive
waste management is established taking into account the operational capability for the
management of radioactive waste and an independent regulatory capability for its
overview. The nuclear waste management practices are on par with international
practices following the guide lines of the International Atomic Energy Agency.
Utmost emphasis is given to separation/recovery of radio-isotopes present in waste for
their deployment for societal application, waste volume minimization, effective
containment and isolation of radio-activity followed by near zero discharge of
radioactivity to the environment.
In this regard:
(i) Ceasium-137, a prominent fission product, has been recovered in large quantity from
nuclear waste and deployed for blood irradiator in non-dispersive glass form.
(ii) Extraction of Stronium-90, another fission product, from nuclear waste could be
demonstrated at laboratory scale using indigenously developed novel extractants.
Stronium-90 has been extracted in small quantity and deployed for generation of
Yttrium-90, which has use for radiotherapy in medical application. The novel extractant
is being manufactured in bulk amount to recover Stronium-90 in larger quantity for its
utilisation as heat source in space applications.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee commends the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre for contributing in ensuring
food and health security of the Nation and recommends to BARC to execute its strategy to

7

BARC is  actively involved in the  production of breeders’ seeds and foundation seeds

Vidyalaya, Jabalpur has taken up the pulses seed production of BARC varieties on a very

Sciences, Raichur, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishva Vidyalaya, Raipur and Dr. G. B. Pant

BARC is  now actively conducting various programmes for food merchants, fruits and

withdrawal of use of fumigants in the  next few years on international level. These

3.  Solid Waste Management
Nisargruna :
BARC has entered into  MOU with Municipal Corporations of Mumbai, Chennai,
Tuticorin, Rajkot, Chandigarh and Delhi Zoo to proactively install the Nisargruna plants and
prove the technology in their premises. Many of these plants are already in place and working

supporting these efforts.
Sludge Hygienisation :
BARC has Developed radiation technology for Dry sewage sludge hygienisation. First of
its kind in India, the fully automatic facility can hygienise 100 tonnes of dry sludge every day.

Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that setting up of Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor, the second

Action Taken by Government
The recommendation of the honorable Committee is noted. The following are further
submitted :-
Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) internals have been kept in poised condition for pre-
heating prior to Sodium filling in Main V essel. BHA VINI  would start the process of Sodium filling
as sodium is the coolant in this reactor. This activity will be followed by fuel loading for
approaching towards first criticality. Initially there could be zero power and power would be
stepped up gradually. Essential physics experiments at low  and high power levels need to be done
to reach the 100% power ultimately. Being first-of-its-kind reactor in the country, many
unanticipated safety and regulatory requirements are emerging in various stages of commissioning
that are being met to make the reactor operation safe. With this all efforts are being made to make

Application for sequential commissioning has been submitted to Atomic Energy Regulatory Board
(AERB).

Recommendation
The Committee recommends that the Department should make concerted efforts to tap Nuclear
Energy to surmount the rising energy need of emerging India. The Department at the same time
must do away with the deficiencies in the realm of safety framework so as to make the nation safe
from nuclear accidents. (Para 19.5)
Action Taken by Government
V arious useful and important suggestions made by the honorable Committee is noted.
Safety is accorded utmost priority in all phases of Nuclear Power Plants (NPPs) from sitting,
design, construction, commissioning and operation. The nuclear power reactors are provided with
multi-layer safety provisions and series of physical barriers to prevent the release of radioactivity
beyond acceptable limits and thereby protect the personnel, public, and the environment.
The safety aspects of the nuclear power reactors to be set up in the country are extensively
reviewed at every stage by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), and the reactors are set
up and operated strictly in accordance with its stage-wise clearances. The operation of nuclear
power plants is carried out by highly trained and licensed personnel, strictly in line with the
approved procedures and technical specifications.
Safety is not static and improvements/ upgrades are effected in NPPs based on evolving
global standards, events and operating experience feedback. Multitier safety reviews by AERB
during all phases of NPPs is in place. Further, review of Indian NPPs by OSART- IAEA has also
been done. The feedbacks obtained from such reviews are suitably incorporated in all the Indian
nuclear reactors as appropriate.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences
on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Eighty-fourth Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the
Demands for Grants (2016-17) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which was presented to both
the Houses of Parliament on 9th May, 2016. There were eighteen recommendations in the Report
of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee was received
from the Ministry on 14th June, 2016. The Committee, on examination of Action Taken Notes, is
not satisfied with action taken by the Ministry in respect of five recommendations (para 4.6, 8.2,
9.2, 12.5 and 15.3) and would like the Ministry to take further action in respect of such
recommendations as indicated in the Report.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on
the action taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:-
FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF THE MINISTRY AND BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR
2016-17
Recommendation
The Committee notes that although there has been a reduction in the budgetary allocation at
RE stage in 2015-16, the Ministry has not been able to utilize the allocated amount optimally and
much amount had remained unspent. The Committee, therefore, recommends that such
underutilization by the Ministry should be avoided and whatever amount is allocated should be
utilized to the fullest extent. (Para 4.2)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry noted the recommendation and will make every effort to utilize fully the allocated
funds.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to know the steps taken in this
direction.
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the Ministry still requires additional funds in the ‘Plan’ component
in order to pursue important programmes and activities in 2016-17 which had been deferred
previously due to paucity of funds. The Committee also notes that the ‘Plan’ component in any
budgetary allocation is important to carry out programmes and activities. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the additional funds for the flagship programmes of the Ministry should be
allocated to the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should be provided
adequate additional amount, as requested by the Ministry, so that the critical programmes are not
adversely affected. (Para 4.6)

2
Action Taken by Government
Ministry would like to thank the Committee for making a recommendation for additional fund
allocation for implementation of the flagship programmes and to meet the critical minimum
requirement without adversely affecting the programmes.
Comments
The Committee notes that the reply of the Ministry does not indicate whether it has
taken any action on the recommendation of the Committee.  The Committee would like to
know the action taken by the Ministry in pursuance of the Committee’s recommendations.
POLAR SCIENCES AND CRYOSPHERE
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the programme is extremely significant from the environmental
aspect as it is through this programme that India’ s presence in Arctic and Antarctica region will
be felt. Further, the study of climate of Polar regions will help in its research of understanding
the climate of cold and fragile region of Himalayas in the wake of climate change. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should undertake more studies and activities in the Polar
regions and should take up this programme sincerely. (Para 6.5)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry of Earth Sciences would like to thank the Committee for the encouragement and
would like to assure that the more studies and activities will be taken up in Polar regions.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. The Committee would like to be apprised about the
roadmap, if any, prepared by the Ministry in this direction and the strategic policy
interventions being contemplated thereon.
Recommendation
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should undertake a realistic assessment
of all the formalities involved in the programme and take action accordingly so that
underutilization of funds is avoided. The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation to the new
rationalized programme, ‘P ACER’  has been reduced in 2016-17 and hopes that the reduction would
not affect the targets of the programme. (Para 6.6)
Action Taken by Government
It may kindly be noted that the reduction in the funds for 2016-17 is primarily due to
postponement of acquisition of Polar Research Vessels in view of technical difficulties.  However,
the reduction does not affect the ongoing scientific programmes of PACER being carried out
currently with the existing infrastructural facilities.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.

3
SEISOMOLGICAL AND GEOSCIENCE (SAGE) PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the funds were underutilized in 2015-16 primarily due to
postponement of construction of building of National Centre for Seismology. The Committee feels
that the Ministry should not have postponed the construction of National Centre for Seismology
causing underutilization of funds which could have been avoided and the progress of projects would
not have been affected. (Para 7.6)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry noted the recommendation and will make every effort to utilize fully the allocated
funds.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and also would like the Ministry to constantly
monitor the utilization of the funds.
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the activities in the main phase have been initiated by the Ministry
and hopes that the drilling process would be started. The Committee recommends that the Ministry
should complete the drilling process within the scheduled time period to enrich its prediction of the
regular occurrence of the earthquake in the region. The Committee also recommends to undertake
scientific drilling programme in other parts of India facing regular occurrence of earthquakes.
(Para 7.11)
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry will make every effort to complete the planned scientific drilling of boreholes
in the Koyna area within the scheduled period. After successful completion of borehole
measurements, instrumentation of the borehole with multiple sensors, and studies on cores/cuttings
in the Koyna region, the expertise thus acquired will be utilized to conduct such activities in other
parts of the country. In the interim, efforts will be made to identify and prioritize other areas in
India where scientific drilling would be necessary.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised about the progress made
by the Ministry in the matter.
NATIONAL CENTRE FOR SEISMOLOGY
Recommendation
In its previous reports (Report Nos. 243 and 260), the Committee had recommended for early
creation of manpower, posts, infrastructure etc. for National Centre for Seismology. The Committee,
however, notes that even after a period of more than four years, the Ministry is still in process
of creation of manpower . Although the land for the construction of building has been identified,
the construction of the building is yet to be taken up. The Committee finds that the approach of

4
the Ministry in the matter is extremely lethargic. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Ministry should initiate the process of construction of the building of National Centre for
Seismology without any further delay. (Para 8.2)
Action Taken by Government
Soon after setting up of National Centre for Seismology in October 2014, a proposal was
prepared and submitted to Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance for creation of
manpower. The proposal is under consideration of Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.
Ministry noted the recommendation. Ministry has initiated the process to identify the related agency
for construction of National Centre for Seismology building.
Comments
The Committee is at a loss to decipher the delay being caused in the creation of
manpower and recommends that the Ministry should actively pursue the matter with the
Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.  The Committee also recommends that the
Ministry should setup a time frame by which the construction of National Centre for
Seismology building is to be completed.
MICROZONATION OF CITIES
Recommendation
The Committee observes that the Microzonation of cities falling in seismic zone of V , IV and
III has been taken up by the Ministry and is working in coordination with GSI. The Committee
recommends that Microzonation of these cities should be carried out expeditiously in view of the
vulnerability of India to severe earthquakes. (Para 9.2)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry has noted the recommendation and would make every effort to complete the
microzonation work in selected most vulnerable areas of the country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to know what concrete action has been
taken by the Ministry to carry out the above task.  Also, the Ministry should fix a timeline
for completing this task.
OCEAN SERVICES, TECHNOLOGY  OBSERV ATIONS, RESOURCES MODELLING AND
SCIENCE (O-STORMS)
Recommendation
The Committee notes the initiatives planned to be taken by the Ministry in 2016-17 and the
amount of expenditure incurred in 2015-16. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would diligently
and prudently work towards these initiatives. The Committee also notes that the Ministry has failed
to acquire Ocean Research Vessels in last four years which is significant for conducting oceanic
research despite the Committee’ s repeated recommendations in its previous reports (Report Nos. 243
and Report No. 260). The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should make all out
efforts to ensure that such vessels are acquired at the earliest. (Para 10.4)

5
Action Taken by Government
Ministry has noted the recommendations and will explore the possibility of acquisition of
research vessels towards replacement of the existing vessels as proposed in the 12th Five Year
Plan.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be informed of the progress made
in the matter.
POLYMETALLIC NODULES AND GAS HYDERATES
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the progress made in harnessing polymetallic nodules and the
explorations being carried out by the Ministry which is significant for economic and strategic
purpose. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should continue with the
exploration and also to develop the deep sea mining system. The Committee also notes the
experiment being carried out for feasibility of extracting gas from gas hydrates and recommends
that the Ministry should continue with experiments in this field. (Para 11.5)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry has noted the recommendation and would continue with exploration of nodules and
phase-wise development of mining system. Similarly, the Ministry will continue its effort for
experimentation towards extraction of gas from hydrates.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee observes that not much progress has been made by the Ministry in acquiring new
dedicated research vessels for the exploration. The Committee also notes that only one research vessel
i.e. Samudra Ratnakar has been deployed. The Committee therefore, recommends that the Ministry
should prudently undertake the acquiring of new vessel and these vessel(s) should be deployed,
without which the exploration of poly metallic sulphides is not feasible. (Para 11.7)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry has noted the recommendations and will explore the possibility of acquisition of
research vessels towards replacement of the existing vessels as proposed in the 12th Five Year
Plan.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be informed of the progress made
in the matter.
Recommendation
The Committee notes the increase in allocation at R.E. stage in 2015-16 and in B.E. 2016-

6
17 and exhorts the Ministry to achieves its targets and undertake the schemes/programmes essential
for studying monsoon and climate change and for forecasting experiments. (Para 12.5)
Acton Taken by the Department
Noted.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be informed of the action taken in
the matter.
HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTING (HPC)
Recommendation
The Committee notes that on the one hand, the available BE of
 ` 10 crore for the programme
in 2015-16 was reduced to  ` 0.50 crore at RE stage and on the other hand the Ministry is not able
to upscale the High Performance Computing due to non-availability of funds. The Committee is of
the view that replies given by the Ministry are contradictory and recommends that the Ministry should
first utilize the funds available at its disposal and then complain about the lack of funds. The
Committee also recommends that sincere efforts be made for achieving augmentation of High
Performance Computing to the level of 10 Peta flop in time bound manner . (Para 13.7)
Action Taken by Government
Noted the recommendations of the Committee towards augmentation of High Performance
Computing Systems. Since HPC Augmentation program of MoES requires  ` 517.47 crores, the
necessary steps are being undertaken to procure the system in a phased manner.  As each step
requires several rounds of deliberations, therefore only  ` 10 crores was budgeted at BE stage of
2015-16 primarily for purchase of diesel for running HPC (24 X 7) at NCMWF due to the
inadequate power load. As the power load was increased from 1MW to 2MW, the requirement of
diesel was not felt leading to inadequate expenditure.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like the Ministry to make realistic
assessment of funds so that underutilization of funds is avoided.
ACCURACY IN WEATHER FORECASTING
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the efforts being made by the Ministry to improve its efficiency
in weather forecasting which is essential in the wake of climate change and unpredictable weather
phenomena. The Committee, however , feels that much more still needs to be done to improve the
accuracy and to bring it at par with international standards. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Ministry should improve its weather forecasting capacities and the upscaling of High
Performance Computing and should also go for collaboration with other nations having well
equipped and advanced weather forecasting systems. (Para 14.5)

7
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Efforts are continuously made to optimize the level of efficiency of the forecasting
system services in terms of accuracy, lead time and associated impact. Government has initiated
a comprehensive Program by upgradation of (i) observation systems (ii) advanced data assimilation
tools (iii) advanced communication and IT infrastructure (iv) high performance computing systems
and (v) intensive/sophisticated training of ESSO- IMD personnel to facilitate the implementation of
advanced global/regional/ meso-scale prediction models for improving the accuracy of weather
forecasts. The performance evaluation of the updated global/meso-scale forecast systems for the
past 5 years have demonstrated enhanced forecast skill. India is a member of World Meteorological
Organisation (WMO) which is a specialised agency of United Nation wherein collaborative
mechanism with international organisations like   UK Meteorological Office (UKMO), National
Centre for Environmental Prediction (NCEP), USA etc. exists for technological exchange to
operational forecasts.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
WATER DESALINATION PLANTS
Recommendation
The Committee commends the establishment of water desalination plants by MoES-NIOT in
Kavaratti, Minicoy and Agatti islands of UT of Lakshadweep, constructed with indigenous
components by using limited infrastructure available in these remote islands. These plants are
greatly catering to the need of fresh quality drinking water in these remote islands and are
extremely cost effective. However , the projects for similar plants at other six islands i.e. Amini,
Chetlet, Kadamat, Kalpeni, Kiltan and Androth, which were conceptualised in the year 2013, are
still hanging fire and mired in administrative procedures. Keeping in view the need for fresh water
in these remote islands for human consumption, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should
coordinate with all the concerned Ministries so that all procedural formalities for the establishment
of the water desalination plants at the six islands are completed at the earliest and the work on
the projects begins without any further delay. (Para 15.3)
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry would endeavor that no delay occurs from NIOT in providing technical support
and expediting the approval process.
Comments
The Committee finds the reply of the Ministry evasive and lacking information on any
concrete action taken by it for coordinating with other concerned Ministries for
completation of formalities for establishment of water desalination plants at the other six
islands.  The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress in the matter during
examination of Demands for Grants 2017-18 of the Ministry.

8
AGRO-METEOROLOGICAL SERVICES
Recommendation
The Committee observes that the number of farmers receiving agro-meteorological advisories
is still small as compared to the total number of farmers in the country. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that efforts should be made in increasing the number of farmers benefiting from
meteorological advisories and enhancing dissemination through various media channels. The
Committee feels that awareness about the agro-met services is necessary and recommends to
continue creating awareness so that more and more farmers get benefited. (Para 16.4)
Action Taken by Government
Ministry would like to thank the Committee for encouragement and would make every effort
to increase the awareness of agro-met services. We are preparing a road map and strategy to
improve on dissemination process and to reach more and more farmers with our forecasts and
warnings.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of the developments in
the matter.
RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND TRAINING OUTREACH
Recommendation
The Committee notes the significance of creating specialized manpower in the field of Earth
System Science and conducting training programmes with participants from across the globe. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should create world class infrastructure
including training schools and hostels and complete the construction of International student Hostel
within the scheduled time frame. The Committee further recommends to enhance extramural
activities and fulfilling the objectives of the programme. (Para 17.5)
Action Taken by Government
The International training hostel to be jointly used by IITM and IMD is being constructed and
will be completed by July 2016. Towards strengthening the training programmes for the scientists
in India and other countries, apart from the WMO Training Schools at IMD and IITM, an
International Training Centre for Operational Oceanography has been established at INCOIS
Hyderabad.  The Centre will be strengthened with more infrastructural facilities.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
ENVIRONMENT MONITORING AND RESEARCH
Recommendation
The Committee observes that not much has been done by the Ministry to bridge the
substantial research gaps between SAFAR and CPCB. The Committee feels that the coordination

9
between different Ministries is important and therefore recommends to ensure coordination among
concerned Institutions and Ministries which would boost studies and research specially in environment-
related research and development. The Committee also feels that inter-Ministry coordination is
essential without which the benefits of any research activity will not be able to reach the citizens and
to contribute to socio-economic development of the country. (Para 18.3)
Action Taken by Government
Several initiatives have been taken to closely link the science based outcome of SAFAR with
CPCB. In this direction, a joint initiative has been taken by MoES and CPCB/MoEF with other
organizations under the Global Environment Facility (GEF) program which will lead to science
based air quality action plan for selected Metropolitan cities in India. In addition, SAFAR experts
also participated in development of NAQI (National Ambient Air Quality Index) of CPCB. It has also
been discussed that air quality forecasting system of SAFAR system can be adopted by CPCB to
strengthen the Indian Air Quality information Services.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of the developments in
the matter.

Technology, Environment & Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its
behalf, present this Two Hundred Ninety-second Report on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment,

same.
